relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the decoded text buffer later re-encoded and searched by soft magic. For the staged witness, both bytes are copied here into `ubuf` and `ulen` becomes 2.

The `FILE_SEARCH` caller knows the remaining bounded extent of the aliased search window but still calls `file_strncmp()` with only the pattern length `slen` and the flags. On whitespace-compacting rules this leaves the helper no bound for scanning `s2` itself.

ASan sink. `file_strncmp()` calls `strlen(s2)` on the interior search pointer instead of respecting the remaining logical bytes in `ms->search.s_len - idx`, so the read runs off the heap allocation created for the temporary UTF-8 buffer.

edges.evidence: Vulnerable original: magiccheck_search_call.search_ptr == file_strncmp_s2_extent.s2_ptr == 0x602000000630. Fixed original: the last matched pair also preserves pointer identity (0x6020000329b0 == 0x6020000329b0).
Both versions record magiccheck_search_call.ws_enabled == file_strncmp_s2_extent.ws_enabled == 1 on the matched helper call pair.

patch_resolves_note: The fixed original still reaches the whitespace FILE_SEARCH helper path, but its instrumented helper records ws_extent_is_bounded=1 instead of 0, showing that the whitespace scan is now explicitly bounded when the protected event executes.
